headline: Xbox secures exclusive GTA 6 streaming rights, sources say
summary: The deal reportedly makes Xbox Cloud Gaming the only platform to stream Grand Theft Auto VI at launch, potentially attracting PC players.
details: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma hinted at a unique Grand Theft Auto VI move during an employee all-hands. Sources familiar with Microsoft’s plans confirm Xbox has landed exclusive game streaming rights for the highly anticipated title.
This deal reportedly means only Xbox Cloud Gaming will be able to stream Grand Theft Auto VI to players at launch. The exact duration of this exclusive agreement is not yet clear.

The streaming rights news comes as Microsoft prepares to open up Xbox Cloud Gaming with a pay-as-you-go option next month. This is perfectly timed for GTA VI's release, allowing players without a console or those who prefer mobile gaming to stream the game.

Additionally, Microsoft is implementing changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming in November, the same month Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to release. These changes include limiting streaming hours for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and Premium subscribers.

During the same all-hands, Sharma also mentioned that Project Helix, the next generation of Xbox hardware, will be a "family of devices." Microsoft plans to partner with other companies on some of these devices.

topic: ai computing startup lambda raises 4b pre-ipo
headline_marked: [[AI computing startup Lambda to raise $4B]] ahead of planned 2027 IPO
headline: AI computing startup Lambda to raise $4B ahead of planned 2027 IPO
summary: The round values the AI cloud provider at $14.5 billion pre-money, with Coatue Management and Blackstone leading. A large portion of its $50 billion backlog is tied to a single deal with Anthropic.
details: AI computing startup Lambda is reportedly raising up to $4 billion in its last private round before a planned 2027 IPO. This round values the company at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation, with Coatue Management and Blackstone leading the investment, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Lambda's backlog dramatically increased from $15 billion in June to $50 billion by September. However, a substantial $35 billion of this growth is attributed to a single commitment from AI lab Anthropic, secured in late August.

This means Lambda's valuation, which has seen significant growth, is heavily reliant on Anthropic's continued payments. Despite this concentration risk, investors are keen to back companies providing scarce GPU capacity, especially those with large contracts with major AI players.

For 'neocloud' providers like Lambda, the challenge lies not in demand but in the high cost of meeting it. Data center expansions are typically debt-funded, and Lambda recently secured an additional $1 billion in debt last week.

Raising more capital now allows Lambda to set the tone for its eventual IPO pricing and access funds before facing public market scrutiny. The company's IPO, initially planned for this year, was reportedly pushed back to 2027 due to market uncertainty.

Lambda will join other Nvidia-backed neoclouds, such as CoreWeave and Nebius, that depend on their stock performance to finance data center buildouts. British neocloud Nscale also recently filed for an IPO and is expected to begin trading soon.
